readme: WHICH FDC ENTRY IS THIS FOOD - the one call in the rung-2 backfill that a machine may not make. fdc_lookup's doctrine measured identity assertions at 37% false locally, and the first mechanical pass proved it live: the top CORROBORATING candidate for 'Bread Crumbs' was Croutons, for 'Rice' it was rice cakes, for 'Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh' it was chicken BREAST, and for 'Peanuts' it was a candy bar. Every one of those agreed inside tolerance. So agreement is necessary and not sufficient, and this file is the frontier ruling that goes with it: nothing is written to `source` unless it is named here AND the numbers still corroborate. Reviewed against the full curated shelf for all 98 Class A rows, 2026-08-26.

Bread Crumbs.why: the top corroborating candidate was Croutons; this is the actual dry grated crumb entry

Cottage Cheese.why: the shelf's top agreeing rows were cottage cheese WITH VEGETABLES and WITH FRUIT; the stored 88 cal / 11.5 P per 100 g is the 2% milkfat entry

Cucumber.why: the row's own note says with peel, so the peeled entry is the wrong one

Frozen Chopped Spinach.why: unprepared, which is what the recipes weigh

Grits.why: the row is Quaker QUICK grits; the top hit was Quaker INSTANT

Olive Oil.why: the top corroborating candidate was a corn/peanut/olive BLEND

Pasta Shells.why: the shelf for 'shells' returns TOSTADA and TACO shells; this is the dry pasta entry the other pasta rows use

Pasta Shells - jumbo.why: same as Pasta Shells - the shelf returns taco shells

Shredded Carrots.why: shredded is a cut, not a different food

Spaghetti.why: the top corroborating candidate was SPINACH spaghetti

Sugar.why: the top corroborating candidate was turbinado

Toasted Sesame Seeds.why: roasted and toasted, which is what the row's name says

Zucchini.why: includes skin, raw - the top hit was BABY zucchini

Greek Yogurt.why: plain nonfat; the top hit was CHOBANI BLUEBERRY

Green Onions.why: FDC's curated set carries scallion TOPS ONLY, not the whole trimmed onion the recipes use. Stands in, and says so.

Mayonnaise.why: the only corroborating curated entry is a no-cholesterol dressing; Great Value mayonnaise is egg-based. Stands in, and says so.

rejected.Rice: FDC's curated shelf for this term returns rice CAKES and rice CRACKERS, not dry long-grain rice. No curated entry for the food was offered.
rejected.Beef Chuck Roast: every chuck-eye candidate reads 24-27 g protein against the stored 19.6, and the stored row's own note says it is a raw basis reflecting a slow-cooked yield. Two different claims; a person decides.
rejected.Pork Chops: no candidate agrees - the bone-in center loin entries read 167-170 cal against the stored 152.
rejected.Heavy Cream: the stored row reads 0.0 g protein and 6.7 g carbs per 100 g against USDA's 2.8/2.8. That is a real question about the row, not a citation.
rejected.Sweet Whole Kernel Corn: every canned sweet corn entry reads 14.3 g carbs against the stored 11.2.
rejected.Garlic: USDA raw garlic is 149 cal per 100 g against the stored 133.
rejected.Sweet Potatoes: the shelf offers only leaves, canned mash and babyfood - no raw sweet potato entry was returned.
rejected.Reduced Fat Mozzarella: the only agreeing candidate is reduced-fat PROVOLONE.
rejected.Cannellini Beans: the only agreeing candidate is canned PINTO beans.
rejected.Cherry Tomatoes: the only agreeing candidate is CANNED tomatoes packed in juice; the row is fresh.
rejected.Parmesan Cheese: the hard entry disagrees on carbs (3.2 vs 7.1) and the grated entries disagree on protein. No clean answer.
rejected.1/3 Fat Cream Cheese: low-fat cream cheese reads 208 cal / 16.7 g fat against the stored 250 / 21.4.
rejected.Olives: the only candidates returned are OLIVE LOAF (a pork lunch meat) and olive oil.
rejected.Apple: the shelf returns rose-apples, apple strudel, apple croissants and babyfood juice. No raw apple entry.
rejected.Pineapple Chunks: every agreeing candidate is a JUICE or juice blend, not fruit.
rejected.Orange Juice: every agreeing candidate is BABYFOOD juice.
rejected.Fat Free Cottage Cheese: the shelf returns fat-free CREAM, AMERICAN and CHEDDAR cheese - no cottage cheese.
rejected.Fat Free Cheddar: USDA fat-free cheddar reads 7.1 g carbs against the stored 10.7.
rejected.Fat Free Mozzarella: the shelf returns fat-free cream cheese, sour cream and American - no mozzarella.
rejected.Korean glass noodles (dangmyeon): the shelf returns RICE noodles; dangmyeon is sweet-potato starch, a different food.
rejected.Feta Cheese: USDA feta reads 14.2 g protein against the stored 17.9.
rejected.Peanuts: the only candidate returned is a peanut CANDY BAR.
rejected.Ground Turmeric: the stored row reads 0.0 g protein and 0.0 g fat against USDA's 9.7 and 3.2. A real question about the row.
rejected.Red Pepper Flakes: the agreeing-by-name candidates are sweet red PEPPERS, raw; the cayenne spice entry disagrees on protein and fat against a stored 0.0/0.0.
rejected.Ground Allspice: stored 0.0 protein / 0.0 fat / 52.6 carbs against USDA's 6.1 / 8.7 / 72.1.
rejected.Poppy Seeds: stored 35.7 / 35.7 / 35.7 is three identical numbers, which is what a household serving rounded to one decimal does; USDA reads 18.0 P / 28.1 C / 41.6 F.
rejected.Boneless Skinless Chicken Thigh: the entire shelf returned is chicken BREAST. Asking for a thigh returned no thigh.
